entities.name: CPFA
observations: Continuous plasma filtration adsorption is an extracorporeal blood-purification treatment studied in burn sepsis.

entities.name: Burn sepsis
observations: Sepsis complicating burn injury; population in CPFA clinical reports.

entities.name: PMID:25429809
observations: 2014 clinical study treated 30 burn-sepsis patients with two CPFA sessions plus routine care; all survived to discharge and physiologic/inflammatory measures improved, but there was no control group.

entities.name: PMID:29961295
observations: 2018 study assigned 86 severely burned patients with sepsis by random-number table to routine care or routine care plus CPFA (43/group); 28-day mortality was 6.98% versus 25.58%, respectively (P=0.023).

entities.name: PMID:31787473
observations: Retrospective burn-center cohort compared CPFA plus RRT in 39 septic-shock/AKI patients with RRT alone in 87 similar patients; mortality was 51.3% versus 77.1% (P=0.004), with authors noting need for prospective studies.
